newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK TO SAVE RESERVES FOR DEBT PAYMENTS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK TO SAVE RESERVES FOR DEBT PAYMENTS.

text.p: Bulgaria's central bank plans to save its dwindling foreign exchange reserves for the possible introduction of a currency board and for foreign debt payments rather than for propping up the lev, a bank official said.

"The BNB will not react on the tension on the domestic forex market and spend its reserves (for interventions) because it must be prepared to meet pending foreign debt payments and the possible introduction of a currency board," said a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official.

The central bank did not intervene on Wednesday to support the lev on the interbank market, where it fell to a record low of 330 per dollar from 285 on Tuesday, dealers said. The dollar traded near 70 per dollar at the beginning of 1996.

The BNB official, who asked not to be identified, said the bank did not plan to erode its reserves any further to sustain imports, which meant that importers would have to buy foreign currency only from commercial banks.
BNB reserves stood near $541 million at the end of October down from $1.434 billion a year ago, BNB figures show.
Dues to government and bank creditors in the first quarter of 1997 total $300 million or some 30 percent of all debt payments for next year.
The International Monetary Fund proposed setting up a currency board system to restore confidence in the currency, help defeat hyperinflation and boost economic growth.
Under the currency board system, the amount of levs in circulation and banks' minimum required reserves at the central bank must be exactly matched by central bank's forex reserves.
The IMF has twice postponed a crucial $115 million funding tranche since September due to Bulgaria's slow performance in closing down loss-making state enterprises and speeding up privatisation.
